Miroslawiec Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Mirosławiec, Poland

Not demolished. Among the oldest and largest Jewish cemeteries in West Pomerania, this site dates to the 17th century, when Jews first arrived in Mirosławiec fleeing persecution and expulsion from Brandenburg between 1510 and 1573. From 1791 to 1815, the community was led by Rabbi Akiva Eiger — later an assistant rabbi in Poznań and one of the most outstanding halakhic authorities of his era — who also headed the local yeshiva; the community was regarded as having a special, supra-regional significance as a kind of 'matrix' to the Jewish community of Berlin. In its 18th-century heyday, the town held about 1,400 Jews. In 1938, Jewish residents were forced to sell their property and leave the town, and the cemetery was vandalized during Kristallnacht that year.
